questions.explanation: The verb must match its subject in number and person. Gender does NOT affect verb form.
When 'I' means the alphabet character, it is third person singular — use 'is'.
Proper nouns ending in 's' that refer to a single entity take singular verb.
'News' looks plural but is actually singular.

questions.questionText: Each of the students ___ a book.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is always singular — takes singular verb.

questions.questionText: Neither Ravi nor his friends ___ present.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject (friends = plural).
Collective nouns take singular verb when acting as a unit.

questions.questionText: Every boy and every girl ___ present.
questions.explanation: Two singular subjects joined by 'and' with 'every' before each take singular verb.

questions.questionText: The United States ___ a large country.
questions.explanation: Names of countries, even with 'States', are singular.

questions.questionText: Bread and butter ___ a common breakfast.
questions.explanation: When two nouns refer to one idea/concept, the verb is singular.
'Scissors' is always plural (like 'trousers', 'glasses').
Subjects ending in 'ics' (mathematics, physics, economics) are singular.

questions.questionText: The boys ___ playing in the garden.
questions.explanation: 'Boys' is plural — takes 'are'.
Two subjects joined by 'and' take plural verb.

questions.questionText: Either the teacher or the students ___ responsible.
questions.explanation: With 'either...or', verb agrees with the nearer subject (students = plural).
'Jury' is singular when acting as one unit.

questions.questionText: Five miles ___ a long distance to walk.
questions.explanation: Distance, time, and money are treated as singular.
Amounts of money are singular.

questions.questionText: The police ___ looking for the thief.
questions.explanation: 'Police' is always plural.
'Everybody' is always singular.
'No one' is always singular.
'Furniture' is an uncountable noun — always singular.
'A number of' is always plural.
'The number of' is always singular.

questions.questionText: He as well as his friends ___ going.
questions.explanation: 'As well as' does not make the subject plural — verb agrees with 'He'.
'Children' is plural.
With either...or, verb agrees with the nearer subject (I → am).
'Book' is singular.
'Water' is uncountable — singular verb.
'Students' is plural — plural verb.
Distance is treated as singular.
